findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "market.crypto" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: social.profile_lookup · Private data: network.blocknumber, network.gas_info, network.token_info, network.token_price, network.prepare_transfer, weather.forecast, market.crypto, web3.lookup, travel.search, places.lookup, social.profile_lookup · Public sink: network.gas_info, network.prepare_transfer, places.lookup · Destructive: places.lookup.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: social.profile_lookup · Private data: network.blocknumber, network.gas_info, network.token_info, network.token_price, network.prepare_transfer, weather.forecast, market.crypto, web3.lookup, travel.search, places.lookup, social.profile_lookup · Public sink: network.gas_info, network.prepare_transfer, places.lookup · Destructive: places.lookup

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
